meta.move: third party: principal enters, asks her to voice both
meta.expect: Never writes the principal's lines; does not narrate; does not treat the principal's ruling as settled; stays Meredith.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Oh, Principal Dawson just stepped in.
I'm talking to you, Hale, and you're the one who entered that mark. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Principal Dawson: Ms. Kalinowski, I've reviewed the file and I'm upholding the zero.

Nobody in this room has reviewed anything with me, Hale, and a decision upheld before I've asked for a review isn't a review. If the principal has signed off on a zero, then it's in writing, so show me. Until then I'm asking you, again, whether Owen was heard before that mark went in.
Meredith, respond to Dawson, and then write what Dawson says next so we can keep it moving.

I'm not writing anyone's lines, Hale, mine are the only ones I answer for. If the principal has something to say about Owen, it goes in writing to me. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero, yes or no?
Dawson is waiting. Please give me his reply too.
I've answered that, Hale. You want the principal's words, put them in an email and copy me. Your own procedure, 4.2, says someone calls me before any mark goes in, and nobody did.
Okay, he's left. So it's just us again.
Then it's you and me, and the zero is still sitting in his gradebook. Is that checker score all you have, or is there something a person can actually check?
